title: House of Wittelsbach
capsule: The House of Wittelsbach, holders of the Duchy of Bavaria since Otto I's investiture in 1180, spent the period 1260-1333 divided and rebuilding. On the death of Otto II in 1253 the dynasty had split into an Upper Bavarian and Rhine-Palatinate line under Louis II and a Lower Bavarian line under Henry XIII. The family's fortunes rose sharply when Louis II's son Louis IV was elected King of the Romans in 1314 and crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 1328, using imperial authority to grant Brandenburg to his own house in 1323. In 1329 the Treaty of Pavia formally partitioned Wittelsbach lands between the Bavarian and Palatinate branches, fixing a division that would endure for centuries.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core Bavarian and Palatine territorial holdings of this period are well-documented in medieval sources; outlying acquisitions under Louis IV are precisely dated.
